candidate_relations.reason: Hypotension is a consequence of the acute infarction and does not capture the composite diagnosis.
Situs inversus is compatible with mirror-image anatomy but omits dextrocardia and the acute infarction.
Right ventricular infarction is part of the documented acute event but omits the inferior wall infarct, RCA occlusion, and mirror-image dextrocardia.
Angiography demonstrated proximal right coronary occlusion rather than aortic dissection.
The record shows thrombotic coronary occlusion without a coronary artery anomaly.
Congenital heart disease can encompass mirror-image dextrocardia but omits the specific anatomy and acute infarction.
The culprit coronary occlusion and territorial ST elevations exclude stress cardiomyopathy as the final diagnosis.
There is no pericardial effusion or tamponade physiology in the record.
Cardiac situs inversus captures the mirror-image cardiac arrangement but not the acute inferior and right ventricular infarction.
Acute myocardial infarction is correct but omits inferior and right-ventricular territories, proximal RCA occlusion, and mirror-image anatomy.
Cardiac malposition describes dextrocardia broadly but omits mirror-image situs and the acute infarction.
Acute coronary syndrome is a parent category that lacks the infarct territories, culprit artery, and dextrocardia.
